why: I15-A (builder A): the prereg toy fixture (f827be4) predates the audit fix F-M2-26 (2940a10, merged after the prereg), under which an M2+ model (holon.gen.machine.Machine(m2plus=True); every milestone after M1, the test milestone T15 included) takes its permissions from the permission guards and raises a label/guard disagreement when actions with the same guard key carry different labels. The toy's commit, finalize, challenge and send (label anyone) and wait (label environment) all lack a caller input and a permission guard, so they form one guard class with two labels: neither `holon run --milestone T15` nor the T15 instrumented model could be built at all (FactsError: principal classes). The one change: wait's principal label environment -> anyone, so the class has one name. No guard, input, effect, span, reason or state changes, so no site, hit, obstruction, law id or expected outcome of TestToyDerivation / TestToyOutcomes moves (labels name a class only; no search policy reads them). Question for the human: the same pattern breaks I13's tests_m2/fixtures/sorts/time_plus_time.json and I14's tests_m2/fixtures/evidence/machine/toy_machine.json under F-M2-26; whether the rule should accept anyone and environment labels on caller-less actions is the lead's call (holon/diagram/principals.py is unchanged here).

I15-A (builder A): the expected model above the ghost marker was written as Machine(facts, path).generate(sha, reach=True), the M2 model at the prereg (f827be4). The audit fix F-M2-26 (2940a10) made the model holon builds for an M2+ run Machine(.., m2plus=True): permissions from the permission guards and one perm_<class> per principal class (holon.mpipeline.milestone_model, CompiledMachine.build(reach=True)). The contract (docstring) is unchanged: the text before the marker is exactly the model holon generates for that run without sites; the one line now builds that model (m2plus=True). Every other assertion (one marker, site_/hit_ per law, nothing above the marker names a ghost definition, Bend checks the file) is kept.

I15-A (builder A): the contract lists an obstruction's registers sorted by var, and I15-P6 and R11 (TestPredictedDerivation.test_coherence_obstructions_at_the_enq_first_call_sites, TestObstructions.test_obstructions_follow_rule_r11) check that name order ([qlen, qpend]). I13's rename maps qpend -> zz_e and qlen -> zz_f, which reverses their order, so a derive that sorts by var (as the contract demands) lists [zz_e, zz_f], i.e. [qpend, qlen] once renamed back, and the order-sensitive JSON comparison of this test failed although every obstruction, register, sort, label, writer set, kappa, rho, at, span, via and constrains was equal under the renaming (checked: it was the only difference). No order of the registers is both sorted by var and invariant under a renaming. The one change: both sides re-sort registers by var after renaming back (by_var); everything else is compared as before.

I15-A (builder A, resumed): the earlier I15 line for this key (wait's principal label environment -> anyone) is withdrawn and the fixture is restored byte for byte to its prereg content (f827be4). The lead's merge fix c8f3fd8 (holon/diagram/principals.py: environment actions form their own guard class, F-M2-26 x I14), merged into the I15 branch, removes the foundation conflict that line worked around: with the prereg fixture, the T15 model (Machine(m2plus=True)) builds again, and TestToyDerivation (both tests) and tests_m2/test_sort_site_ghost.py::TestToyGhost pass. why: I15-B (builder B): the prereg (f827be4) asserts that an UNKNOWN SORT-site record has scope 'bounded' (contract: 'Otherwise UNKNOWN with the bound (scope bounded)'). The audit fix F-M2-01 (FX1, merged after the prereg; holon.mpipeline.scope_fields, spec/schemas/result_record_v2.schema.json allOf '0.3 records: scope comes from statement.scope, never from the status') makes a holon-ir/0.3 record's scope its statement's, and the v2 schema then REQUIRES scope 'unbounded' for a statement whose scope is unbounded, as every SORT-site law's is. The first test asserts both v2 validity and scope 'bounded', which no 0.3 record can satisfy; giving UNKNOWN site records scope 'bounded' (or dropping statement_scope) would undo F-M2-01 for one rule. The one change, in both tests: scope must equal the statement's scope kind ('unbounded' here), and r['bound'] (the search bound, which F-M2-01 keeps in its own field) must be non-empty (already asserted by the second test; added to the first). Status UNKNOWN, no witness at any entry point, every entry UNKNOWN with a bound and scope v2 validity are asserted as before. Reported under Surprises and Questions for the human.

I15-B (the I15 line of this file about the UNKNOWN scope assertion, re-keyed per test): the assertion r['scope'] == 'bounded' for an UNKNOWN record cannot hold together with this test's own v2 validation, since the audit fix F-M2-01 (FX1, after the prereg) makes a holon-ir/0.3 record's scope its statement's and the v2 schema then requires scope 'unbounded' for a statement scope unbounded (every SORT-site law's). Now: scope equals the statement's scope kind, and r['bound'] (the search bound F-M2-01 keeps in its own field) is non-empty. Every other assertion is unchanged.

I15-B (I15-P2's check; same conflict with F-M2-01 as TestRecords.test_every_m2_law_has_a_record_valid_under_v1_and_v2): r['scope'] == 'bounded' becomes r['scope'] == the statement's scope kind ('unbounded'); status UNKNOWN, a non-empty bound, witnesses at every entry point, each UNKNOWN with no witness, are asserted as before. The predicted status is unchanged; only the meaning of the record field scope moved (F-M2-01).
